verifications.llm_reasoning: The current mapping is close but too intervention-specific: WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE describes PD-1 blockade therapy, whereas the original pathway name and rationale refer to the underlying inhibitory signaling biology of the PD-1/PD-L1 axis (PD-1 engagement, SHP-mediated suppression of TCR/CD28 signaling, and reversal by blockade). Among the candidates, REACTOME_CO_INHIBITION_BY_PD_1 is the best conceptual match and has higher priority than WikiPathways. No HALLMARK pathway captures this mechanism equally well.

WP_T_CELL_RECEPTOR_AND_COSTIMULATORY_SIGNALING accurately captures the described biology of TCR recognition plus CD28 co-stimulation, which is the core process underlying PD-1/PD-L1 blockade responsiveness. Although Reactome candidates are more specific to CD28 biology, the current WikiPathways mapping already represents the combined TCR and co-stimulatory signaling concept well and is not clearly wrong.

The original pathway name and rationale are specifically about IFN-γ (type II interferon) signaling through JAK/STAT components, which is more precise than the broad WikiPathways term 'Interferon-mediated signaling' that can include type I and other interferon responses. Among the candidates, REACTOME_INTERFERON_GAMMA_SIGNALING is the best semantic match and is higher-priority than WikiPathways. HALLMARK_IL2_STAT5_SIGNALING and HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING are not appropriate because they describe different cytokine pathways.

The current mapping to WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE is related to checkpoint therapy response, not the core biology of the original pathway. The original name and rationale describe MHC-I antigen processing/presentation: endogenous antigen processing, HLA-I loading, and presentation to CD8+ T cells. Among the provided candidates, GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION_OF_ENDOGENOUS_ANTIGEN is the closest semantic and biological match. Although GO has lower priority than Reactome/KEGG/Hallmark, no higher-priority candidate capturing MHC-I antigen presentation is present, so this correction is warranted.

The current mapping is incorrect: 'Amplification and expansion of oncogenic pathways as metastatic traits' describes metastatic oncogenic signaling, which is unrelated to tumor mutational burden/neoantigen load. The original pathway is about immunogenicity from high mutation burden and response to checkpoint blockade, so an immunotherapy pathway is a much better semantic match. Among the candidates, WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE best captures the NSCLC/atezolizumab context and the neoantigen/TMB-driven checkpoint inhibitor biology.

The original pathway describes a VEGF/TGF-β-driven immunosuppressive stroma that excludes CD8+ T cells and contributes to immunotherapy resistance. The current WikiPathways mapping is pancreatic-cancer-specific and focuses on T cell modulation/desmoplasia, which is related but narrower and less directly aligned with the stated VEGF/TGF-β biology. Among the candidates, HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING is the highest-priority and best semantic match to the TGF-β-driven stromal immunosuppressive context.

verifications.Original Pathway Name: Myeloid‑derived suppressor cells / Treg and immunosuppressive cytokines
verifications.llm_reasoning: The current GO term captures only one consequence of the biology—suppression of T-cell responses to tumor cells—but the original pathway name and rationale emphasize a broader immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment driven by myeloid-derived suppressor cells, Tregs, and suppressive cytokines such as TGF-β. Among the provided candidates, a term centered on regulatory T-cell biology better matches the core mechanism than a generic negative regulation of T-cell anti-tumor immunity. No higher-priority HALLMARK/REACTOME option is available in the candidate list, so the best correction from the provided choices is GOBP_REGULATORY_T_CELL_DIFFERENTIATION.

The current mapping to PD-1 blockade is not the best match for the original pathway name, which centers on KRAS/STK11/KEAP1-linked metabolic and immune biology in NSCLC. The rationale emphasizes KRAS-driven tumor biology and the effects of STK11/KEAP1 co-mutations on immune suppression and metabolic reprogramming, not the PD-1 pathway itself. Among the candidates, HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP is the highest-priority and most directly relevant curated hallmark set capturing KRAS activation biology, making it a better MSigDB mapping than a PD-1 blockade pathway.

The original pathway describes a B-/T-cell–inflamed transcriptional program (NMF4) characterized by pre-existing adaptive immune activation, PD-L1 elevation, and response to checkpoint blockade. WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE is mechanistically related but is an intervention-specific pathway, not the underlying biology of an inflamed tumor microenvironment. Among the provided candidates, GOBP_POSITIVE_REGULATION_OF_ADAPTIVE_IMMUNE_RESPONSE best captures the core biology of coordinated B- and T-cell immune activation. No higher-priority HALLMARK/REACTOME option is present in the candidate list, so this GO term is the best available correction.

The original pathway describes the SCLC-I inflamed subtype gene program in small cell lung cancer, with immune activation/CD8A/B features and immunotherapy response. WP_NONSMALL_CELL_LUNG_CANCER is biologically mismatched because it refers to NSCLC rather than SCLC. Among the candidates, KEGG_SMALL_CELL_LUNG_CANCER is the most directly relevant and more appropriate than the current mapping; no higher-priority HALLMARK pathway captures this specific lung cancer subtype program better.
